turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: One hundred and forty-nine! Good heavens! Is that all? It appears my nephew, Lord Illingworth, occupies numbers 151 and 153. I trust you are not in the habit of disturbing his repose?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Good heavens, no! I wouldn't dream of it, Lady Bracknell. I assure you, I'm exceedingly mindful of the peace and quiet of one's neighbours.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: One hundred and forty-nine! It is almost ludicrously modest, Mr. Worthing. I must confess, I had anticipated a more…substantial address for a gentleman who proposes to enter my family. Do I understand you to say you possess no family tree at all, Mr. Worthing?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: A family tree, Lady Bracknell? Well, that's…a rather delicate matter, actually. I’ve always understood my origins to be… somewhat irregular, if you understand what I mean.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Irregular, you say? My dear Mr. Worthing, irregularity is a most undesirable characteristic, particularly in a gentleman seeking the hand of my daughter. I find I must inquire further into this… *delicate matter* you allude to. Pray, do elaborate.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I… I really hadn't intended to burden you with such a personal detail, Lady Bracknell. It’s a long story, involving a handbag and a railway station, and I fear it’s rather… complicated.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A handbag and a railway station, you say? Mr. Worthing, I confess, my sensibilities are quite reeling! It appears we are dealing with a situation of considerable… *unorthodoxy*. Pray, proceed with this 'long story,' but be assured, I shall require the utmost clarity and, dare I say, a considerable degree of justification should you wish to retain my favour.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: It was rather sudden, you see, Lady Bracknell. I was found, a mere infant, left in a handbag at Victoria Station. My origins are… well, they’re not precisely traceable to a family in the conventional sense.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A handbag, Mr. Worthing? At Victoria Station? Really! It seems my anxieties were entirely justified. I must confess, I find myself rather at a loss for words – a most unusual occurrence, I assure you.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: I… I suppose it’s rather dreadful to admit, Lady Bracknell, but I haven’t the faintest idea who my parents were. I was simply… left. It’s all terribly embarrassing, I assure you, and I’m quite sure it doesn’t reflect on my character.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Left, you say? Abandoned like a discarded glove! Mr. Worthing, I am beginning to suspect that your narrative, while undeniably diverting, lacks a certain… *foundation*. One’s origins, you see, are of paramount importance; they are, in essence, the very bedrock upon which one’s character is built.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Oh, terribly sorry, Lady Bracknell, I didn't mean to cause such a stir! It’s just... the circumstances were rather extraordinary, and I've always tried to be honest, even if the truth is a bit… unconventional. I assure you, I’m a man of good intentions, and I’d never intentionally mislead anyone, especially not you, madam.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Good intentions, Mr. Worthing, are notoriously unreliable. I find myself wondering, are you, perhaps, acquainted with any tradesmen? For I assure you, a connection with the mercantile class is scarcely a foundation upon which to build a respectable marriage.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Tradesmen, Lady Bracknell? Good heavens, no! My… my guardian, the late Mr. Hobbs, was a solicitor, a man of impeccable standing, I assure you. I've always striven to uphold those respectable standards myself.

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: A solicitor, you say? While marginally less objectionable than a butcher, Mr. Worthing, it still leaves a great deal to be desired. I trust, of course, that Mr. Hobbs was not involved in any… *unpleasantness*? One must be exceedingly careful about these legal matters, you understand.

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Unpleasantness? Oh, absolutely not, Lady Bracknell! Mr. Hobbs was the very picture of propriety and… and legal rectitude. I can assure you, he was a man of the highest integrity; I learned everything from him, you see.

turns.speaker: Gwendolen
turns.text: Really, Mama, must you interrogate the poor man so relentlessly? I’ve already declared my engagement to Mr. Worthing, and frankly, his past is of absolutely no consequence to my happiness! I find his sincerity quite charming, don't you agree?

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: My dear Gwendolen, your impulsive declarations are charming, I grant you, but they do not absolve me of my duty to ensure the preservation of decorum. Sincerity, while occasionally agreeable, is hardly a substitute for suitable lineage and, dare I say, demonstrable wealth. Mr. Worthing, I believe we were discussing your family; I trust you haven’t omitted any… *significant* details?

turns.speaker: Jack
turns.text: Significant details? Oh dear, I… I believe my origins are rather commonplace, Lady Bracknell. My parents, you see, were… well, I was found, rather unexpectedly, in a handbag. It’s a rather long story, I’m afraid!

turns.speaker: Lady Bracknell
turns.text: Found in a handbag, you say? Mr. Worthing, really! One has quite enough difficulty in tracing one's pedigree as it is, without resorting to such… *unconventional* circumstances. I daresay this handbag possessed a crest?

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: I am engaged to Mr. Worthing, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Pardon me, you are not engaged to any one. When you do become engaged to some one, I, or your father, should his health permit him, will inform you of the fact. An engagement should come on a young girl as a surprise, pleasant or unpleasant, as the case may be. It is hardly a matter that she could be allowed to arrange for herself . . . And now I have a few questions to put to you, Mr. Worthing. While I am making these inquiries, you, Gwendolen, will wait for me below in the carriage.

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Mamma!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In the carriage, Gwendolen!

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Gwendolen, the carriage!

opening.speaker: Gwendolen
opening.text: Yes, mamma.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: You can take a seat, Mr. Worthing.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Thank you, Lady Bracknell, I prefer standing.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I feel bound to tell you that you are not down on my list of eligible young men, although I have the same list as the dear Duchess of Bolton has. We work together, in fact. However, I am quite ready to enter your name, should your answers be what a really affectionate mother requires. Do you smoke?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, yes, I must admit I smoke.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am glad to hear it. A man should always have an occupation of some kind. There are far too many idle men in London as it is. How old are you?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Twenty-nine.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A very good age to be married at. I have always been of opinion that a man who desires to get married should know either everything or nothing. Which do you know?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I know nothing, Lady Bracknell.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: I am pleased to hear it. I do not approve of anything that tampers with natural ignorance. Ignorance is like a delicate exotic fruit; touch it and the bloom is gone. The whole theory of modern education is radically unsound. Fortunately in England, at any rate, education produces no effect whatsoever. If it did, it would prove a serious danger to the upper classes, and probably lead to acts of violence in Grosvenor Square. What is your income?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Between seven and eight thousand a year.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: In land, or in investments?

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: In investments, chiefly.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: What between the duties expected of one during one’s lifetime, and the duties exacted from one after one’s death, land has ceased to be either a profit or a pleasure. It gives one position, and prevents one from keeping it up. That’s all that can be said about land.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: I have a country house with some land, of course, attached to it, about fifteen hundred acres, I believe; but I don’t depend on that for my real income. In fact, as far as I can make out, the poachers are the only people who make anything out of it.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: A country house! How many bedrooms? Well, that point can be cleared up afterwards. You have a town house, I hope? A girl with a simple, unspoiled nature, like Gwendolen, could hardly be expected to reside in the country.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Well, I own a house in Belgrave Square, but it is let by the year to Lady Bloxham. Of course, I can get it back whenever I like, at six months’ notice.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Lady Bloxham? I don’t know her.

opening.speaker: Jack
opening.text: Oh, she goes about very little. She is a lady considerably advanced in years.

opening.speaker: Lady Bracknell
opening.text: Ah, nowadays that is no guarantee of respectability of character. What number in Belgrave Square?
